=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:25183-25199 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason`, the backstop sets `_spahr_label_age="unknown"` and ends the `merge_lease_wait` hold whenever `_stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes` gives no numeric age and the issue's stall clock is above 2 × STALL_MERGE_LEASE_WAIT_MAX_MINUTES. That age can be missing because of a one-off GraphQL read error (not cached), a cached "none", or a `labeled` event outside the last 50, and all three are treated the same.
  WHY: The stall clock measures the issue's stall, not the label's age, so a PR that got `ai:merge-lease-wait` minutes ago on an issue stalled for more than 48 h loses its hold on one failed read. recover_stalled_issue, invoke_stall_judge (judge_pick hold), retrigger_review, resolve_merge_conflict and `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard` (non-green PRs) then go ahead and can push to or dispatch on a green PR that is waiting for the lease. This breaks the requirement that the wait be "measured from the label's last `labeled` event". Test `test_hold_reason_lease_wait_lapses_on_label_age_and_logs_once` case F encodes this behaviour. Suggested fix: return a separate code for a read error and apply the backstop only to the cached `none`. All reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5277-5298 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `break` after a match was removed from `_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr`, so after the branch or body PR matches, the loop still makes one uncached `_fetch_pr_json` (`pulls/<n>`) call for each lower-numbered cross-ref, up to the 20-fetch cap.
  WHY: This runs on every stall-judge call on every tick, before the lease-hold check can skip it, so the common match case costs up to 20 REST reads per tick instead of 1 (the test fixture has 25 lower-numbered cross-refs). That goes against the §15 constraint that the lookup "adds at most the two `gh pr list` calls". The cost is bounded, so all reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:25192-25193 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The lapse dedupe key `local _spahr_lapse_key="${_spahr_number:-unknown}"` falls back to the shared literal `unknown` when the PR payload has no `.number`, so the first such lapse hides the `STALL_MERGE_LEASE_HOLD_LAPSED` log for every later PR without a number in the same poller process.
  WHY: The lapse itself still works, but operators lose the per-PR log signal. Both reviewers rated it NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same issue as a hardening suggestion.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5277-5298 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The picker orders candidates numerically and swaps to a lower-numbered implementation PR. `_find_all_linked_prs` (line 5152) uses lexicographic `sort -u`, which is the order `close_linked_pr` (lines 20215-20216) works through, so the two can choose different PRs (for example #9999 vs #10000).
  WHY: The judge diagnostics and the picked-PR hold check can name a different PR from the one the close path acts on, so a hold on #10000 will not stop the judge when the picker selects #9999. Rated NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5437-5441 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: In `_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard`, the body close-keyword search (`gh_retry gh pr list`) does not tell a gh command failure apart from a successful search that found no PRs.
  WHY: The behaviour is safe (it refuses with `reason=check_unavailable`), but both cases log the same thing, which makes debugging harder. Rated NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The stall judge's diagnostics describe the issue's own implementation PR whenever one exists."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (invoke_stall_judge / _stall_judge_pick_linked_pr)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: invoke_stall_judge falls back to `_issue_cross_ref_pr_number_last` when `_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr` finds no `implementation` source. The picker does not treat closed implementation PRs as diagnostic candidates, but such a PR may be needed to explain why an issue stalled after its implementation PR was closed unmerged. The reviewer rated it MAJOR.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason, backstop block at lines ~25186-25190 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The backstop treats every unreadable label age the same way, whether it is a one-off GraphQL error (not cached; `gh_retry gh api graphql ... || return 1`) or a cached `none`. Either way the hold lapses once the issue's stall clock is above 2 × STALL_MERGE_LEASE_WAIT_MAX_MINUTES, which is unrelated to the label's age.
  WHY: One transient failure leaves `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason` printing nothing. recover_stalled_issue, the standalone ai:done hold, `_rtr_ai_hold_reason`, `_std_rtr_ai_hold_reason`, resolve_merge_conflict and the judge_pick hold then go ahead and can dispatch a review or push an empty commit to a green PR waiting for the lease, which drops `ai-review/head-gate`. Only close_and_reissue stays protected, by green_head. Fix: return code 2 for a read error and 1 for "none", and apply the backstop only to the cached `none`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr, lines 5277-5281 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: After a branch PR matches, the loop still makes one uncached `_fetch_pr_json` (`pulls/<n>`) call for each lower-numbered cross-ref, up to the 20-fetch cap.
  WHY: A lease-held issue costs up to 20 REST reads per tick instead of 1, which goes against §15. Fix: after a match, fetch only lower-numbered candidates that also appear in `_sjp_branch` or `_sjp_bodyref`.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason lapse dedupe key (around line 25192)
  PROBLEM: The key is the PR number only, falling back to `unknown`, so a backstop lapse or any payload without `.number` hides later STALL_MERGE_LEASE_HOLD_LAPSED lines. Fix: skip the dedupe when `_spahr_number` is empty, or add the age kind to the key.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:module-level mktemp for _STALL_MERGE_LEASE_LAPSE_LOG_FILE / _STALL_MERGE_LEASE_AGE_CACHE_FILE (lines ~25209-25218)
  PROBLEM: The temp files are never removed and pile up on self-hosted or local runs. Fix: remove them in the existing EXIT trap, if there is one.
- HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: A transient GraphQL read error in _stall_merge_lease_label_age_minutes can make the hold lapse at once for an old stalled issue.
  WHY: When the stall clock is past 2 × STALL_MERGE_LEASE_WAIT_MAX_MINUTES, the code sets _spahr_label_age="unknown" and the hold lapses, which can close a green PR that is waiting for the merge lease.

  WHY: The first PR without a number to lapse hides the STALL_MERGE_LEASE_HOLD_LAPSED log for every other one.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_reissue_green_pr_guard lines 5437-5441 (gh_retry gh pr list) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The body close-keyword search does not tell a gh command failure apart from a "no PRs found" result.
  WHY: The behaviour is safe (`reason=check_unavailable`), but both cases log the same error, which makes debugging harder.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr lines 5277-5281 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The picker loop fetches PR payloads for every lower-numbered candidate up to the fetch cap, even after it finds a match.
  WHY: It makes several uncached pulls/<n> calls per judge call per tick, which exceeds the §15 budget of "at most the two gh pr list calls".

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:new backstop block in `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason` (the chunk at lines 25042-25103 in the LAST RUN DIFF) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The backstop fires when the stall clock is above 2 × `STALL_MERGE_LEASE_WAIT_MAX_MINUTES` and there is no numeric age. That covers both a transient GraphQL error and a cached "none" (`ai:merge-lease-wait` not among the last 50 timeline events). The stall clock is unrelated to the label's age.
  WHY: For an issue stalled more than 2 × max with a newly labeled PR, one transient error makes the hold lapse and logs `STALL_MERGE_LEASE_HOLD_LAPSED`. Callers (`recover_stalled_issue`, `invoke_stall_judge`, the guard, the retrigger/resolve paths) then dispatch a review or close_and_reissue on a green PR, which is the failure #9892 aims to prevent. It also breaks the "measured from the label's last `labeled` event" requirement.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lapse dedupe key inside `_stall_pr_ai_hold_reason` (`local _spahr_lapse_key="${_spahr_number:-unknown}"`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A payload without `.number` (possible with the batched GraphQL linked_pr shape that `recover_stalled_issue` passes in) shares the dedupe key `unknown`, so only the first `STALL_MERGE_LEASE_HOLD_LAPSED pr=unknown` line is logged.
  WHY: The lapse still happens, but operators lose the per-PR signal. Fix: use a per-PR surrogate, or skip the dedupe when the number is missing.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_stall_judge_pick_linked_pr`, loop body after the `break` was removed (`if [ -n "${STALL_JUDGE_PICKED_PR}" ] && [ "${_sjp_pr}" -ge "${STALL_JUDGE_PICKED_PR}" ]; then continue; fi`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: After the match, the loop makes one uncached `_fetch_pr_json` (`pulls/<n>`) call per lower-numbered candidate, up to the 20-fetch cap. The fixture `test_stall_judge_pick_tries_branch_hits_before_many_cross_refs` triggers 20 reads instead of 1.
  WHY: The fetch cap is spent on cross-ref-only PRs that cannot replace the match, against §15. Fix: restore `break`, or skip cross-ref-only candidates below the matched branch/body PR.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
